pr_title: [Core] Fix TypedArray encoding when full objects is disabled
pr_body:
Typed arrays containing objects, are now correctly encoded with type `EncodedObjectAsID` when full objects is disabled.

Alternative to #90990
Fixes #90467
Fixes #94384

issue_context.title: Error encoding object typed array with `var_to_bytes` and decoding with `bytes_to_var_with_objects`
issue_context.body:
### Tested versions

- Reproducible in 4.3.dev (regression from #78219)

### System information

Irrelevant

### Issue description

Encoding a (object) typed array with `var_to_bytes` then decoding with `bytes_to_var_with_objects` cause an error.

While this is very uncommon, encoding with `var_to_bytes` and  decoding with `bytes_to_var_with_objects` should always be possible.

### Steps to reproduce

Run the following script:

```gdscript
func _ready():
	var res := ImageTexture.new()
	var my_arr : Array[ImageTexture]
	my_arr.push_back(res)
	print(bytes_to_var_with_objects(var_to_bytes(my_arr)))
```

Notice the error:

```
ERROR: Attempted to push_back an object of type 'EncodedObjectAsID' into a TypedArray, which does not inherit from 'ImageTexture'.
   at: validate_object (core/variant/container_type_validate.h:129)
ERROR: Condition "!_p->typed.validate(value, "push_back")" is true.
   at: push_back (core/variant/array.cpp:285)
```

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

See the script above.

review_comments:
> `Array[EncodedObjectAsID]` may be incompatible with `Array[T]`.

Not sure I understand, this is exactly why when encoding with `p_full_objects = false` we **must** set the serialized array type to to `EncodedObjectAsID` since the content will actually be `EncodedObjectAsID`.
This will cause an error when assigning the array to a typed variable.

I mean, this is expected, you can't encode with `p_full_objects = false` and expect object types to be preserved.

This is the same as doing:

```
var obj := MyOjbect.new()
obj = bytes_to_var(var_to_bytes(obj))
```

You'll get a type error, because you can't encode objects when `p_full_objects = false` so you won't get an object of type `MyObject` out of it when you decode, but an `EncodedObjectAsID`.

This implementation basically has the same behavior as before, you can't encode with `p_full_objects = false`, decode with `p_full_objects = true` and expect the result to have proper typing.

Without this change (i.e. with the current implementation), you'd encode the array as `Array[MyType]`, and the objects as `EncodedObjectAsID`.
Then you'd either decode that with `p_full_objects = false` (where you force the array type to `EncodedObjectAsID`, see [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/core/io/marshalls.cpp#L796), [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/core/io/marshalls.cpp#L808) and [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/master/core/io/marshalls.cpp#L822)), or if you decode with `p_full_objects = true` you'd actually get the error you describe (i.e. decoding will not force the type to `EncodedObjectAsID`, but the objects got encoded as `EncodedObjectAsID` so you'll try to assign `EncodedObjectAsID` to an array of different type).

If anything, this PR makes this work as expected (if you encode with `p_full_objects = false` and decode with `p_full_objects = true` it will not fail, and it shouldn't since that's always safe to do, even if, for obvious reasons, you'll lose the object types).
I've opened https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/94384 showing the other regression (fixed by this PR).
